sets.title: ATMs on a road network
sets.contentHtml:

sets.title: OTT subscribers
sets.contentHtml:
Over the top (OTT) subscribers of a platform are segregated into three categories: i) Kid, ii) Elder, and iii) Others.

Some of the subscribers used one app and the others used multiple apps to access the platform. The figure below shows the percentage of the total number of subscribers in 2023 and 2024 who belong to the ‘Kid’ and ‘Elder’ categories.

(Figure: Kid – 15% in 2023, 20% in 2024; Elder – 20% in 2023, 30% in 2024.)

The following additional facts are known about the numbers of subscribers.

  2. In 2024, 1/2 of the subscribers from the ‘Kid’ category and 2/3 of the subscribers from the ‘Elder’ category subscribers use one app.

sets.title: Air-conditioner modes
sets.contentHtml:
The air-conditioner (AC) in a large room can be operated either in REGULAR mode or in POWER mode to reduce the temperature.

If the AC operates in REGULAR mode, then it brings down the temperature inside the room (called inside temperature) at a constant rate to the set temperature in 1 hour. If it operates in POWER mode, then this is achieved in 30 minutes.

If the AC is switched off, then the inside temperature rises at a constant rate so as to reach the temperature outside at the time of switching off in 1 hour. The temperature outside has been falling at a constant rate from 7 pm onward until 3 am on a particular night. The following graph shows the inside temperature between 11 pm (23:00) and 2 am (2:00) that night.

(Graph, inside temperature in °C: 23:00 – 38, 00:00 – 26, 00:30 – 31, 01:00 – 26, 01:30 – 30, 02:00 – 28, joined by straight lines.)

The following facts are known about the AC operation that night.

  • The AC was turned on for the first time that night at 11 pm (23:00).
  • The AC setting was changed (including turning it on/off, and/or setting different temperatures) only at the beginning of the hour or at 30 minutes after the hour.
  • The AC was used in POWER mode for longer duration than in REGULAR mode during this 3-hour period.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.textHtml: The ATM placed at the (R-C, V2) intersection has a cash requirement of Rs. 9 Lakhs.
The cash requirement of the ATM placed at the (R-C, V2) intersection cannot be uniquely determined.
The ATM placed at the (R-C, V2) intersection has a cash requirement of Rs. 8 Lakhs.
There is no ATM placed at the (R-C, V2) intersection.

questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. All six totals add to 22+20+20 = 62 = 15+21+26. Values are distinct integers from 7 to 15, with 7 and 15 present, so the other four sum to 62 − 22 = 40.

7 and 15 share a road whose total is at least 22: only R-A works (V2 = 21 is too small; V3 = 26 would need a third ATM of 4). So R-A holds exactly 7 and 15.

R-B and R-C each total 20 using values from 8–14: that needs exactly two ATMs each (three would be ≥ 24), i.e. the pairs {8, 12} and {9, 11}. So the six values are 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 15.

Columns: if 15 is at (R-A, V1), V1 = 15 holds nothing else, 7 must be at V3 (7 at V2 would need two more ATMs summing to 14 on V2 — impossible), V2 = 12 + 9 and V3 = 7 + 8 + 11. If 7 is at (R-A, V1), V1 needs an 8 below it, 15 must be at V3 (15 at V2 would need a 6), V3 needs an 11, and V2 = 12 + 9.

Clue 2: 12 must be 12 km from the ATM at (R-C, V3). In both cases this forces 12 at (R-B, V2) (5 + 7 = 12 km), 9 at (R-C, V2) and 11 at (R-C, V3).

CaseR-AR-BR-C
1V1: 15, V3: 7V2: 12, V3: 8V2: 9, V3: 11
2V1: 7, V3: 15V1: 8, V2: 12V2: 9, V3: 11

Answer: A. In both cases the ATM at (R-C, V2) has Rs. 9 Lakhs.

questions.stemHtml:
Which of the following two statements is/are DEFINITELY true?

Statement A: Each of R-A, R-B, and R-C has two ATMs.
Statement B: Each of V1, V2, and V3 has two ATMs.

Both Statement A and Statement B

R-B and R-C each total 20 using values from 8–14: that needs exactly two ATMs each (three would be ≥ 24), i.e. the pairs {8, 12} and {9, 11}. So the six values are 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 15.

Columns: if 15 is at (R-A, V1), V1 = 15 holds nothing else, 7 must be at V3 (7 at V2 would need two more ATMs summing to 14 on V2 — impossible), V2 = 12 + 9 and V3 = 7 + 8 + 11. If 7 is at (R-A, V1), V1 needs an 8 below it, 15 must be at V3 (15 at V2 would need a 6), V3 needs an 11, and V2 = 12 + 9.

Clue 2: 12 must be 12 km from the ATM at (R-C, V3). In both cases this forces 12 at (R-B, V2) (5 + 7 = 12 km), 9 at (R-C, V2) and 11 at (R-C, V3).

CaseR-AR-BR-C
1V1: 15, V3: 7V2: 12, V3: 8V2: 9, V3: 11
2V1: 7, V3: 15V1: 8, V2: 12V2: 9, V3: 11

Answer: D. Every horizontal road has exactly two ATMs in both cases, so Statement A is always true. In case 1, V1 has one ATM and V3 has three, so Statement B is not definitely true.

questions.stemHtml: How many subscribers belonged to the ‘Others’ category in 2024?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. Let the 2023 total be T and let x = Kid multiple-app users = Elder one-app users (2023).

Kid 2023: 10,000 + x = 0.15T. Elder 2023: x + 15,000 = 0.20T. Subtracting: 5,000 = 0.05T, so T = 1,00,000, Kid = 15,000, Elder = 20,000, x = 5,000.

2024: total = 1,10,000; Kid = 20% = 22,000 (11,000 one app, 11,000 multiple); Elder = 30% = 33,000 (22,000 one app, 11,000 multiple); Others = 55,000.

Answer: B. Others 2024 = 1,10,000 × (100 − 20 − 30)% = 55,000.

questions.stemHtml: What percentage of subscribers in the ‘Kid’ category used multiple apps in 2023?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. Let the 2023 total be T and let x = Kid multiple-app users = Elder one-app users (2023).

Kid 2023: 10,000 + x = 0.15T. Elder 2023: x + 15,000 = 0.20T. Subtracting: 5,000 = 0.05T, so T = 1,00,000, Kid = 15,000, Elder = 20,000, x = 5,000.

2024: total = 1,10,000; Kid = 20% = 22,000 (11,000 one app, 11,000 multiple); Elder = 30% = 33,000 (22,000 one app, 11,000 multiple); Others = 55,000.

Answer: C. Kid 2023 = 15,000, of whom 5,000 used multiple apps: 5,000/15,000 = 33.33%.

questions.stemHtml: What was the percentage increase in the number of subscribers in the ‘Elder’ category from 2023 to 2024?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. Let the 2023 total be T and let x = Kid multiple-app users = Elder one-app users (2023).

Kid 2023: 10,000 + x = 0.15T. Elder 2023: x + 15,000 = 0.20T. Subtracting: 5,000 = 0.05T, so T = 1,00,000, Kid = 15,000, Elder = 20,000, x = 5,000.

2024: total = 1,10,000; Kid = 20% = 22,000 (11,000 one app, 11,000 multiple); Elder = 30% = 33,000 (22,000 one app, 11,000 multiple); Others = 55,000.

Answer: B. Elder: 20,000 → 33,000, an increase of 13,000/20,000 = 65%.

Quick check: 1.1 × 30/20 = 1.65.

questions.stemHtml: What could be the minimum percentage of subscribers who used multiple apps in 2024?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. Let the 2023 total be T and let x = Kid multiple-app users = Elder one-app users (2023).

Kid 2023: 10,000 + x = 0.15T. Elder 2023: x + 15,000 = 0.20T. Subtracting: 5,000 = 0.05T, so T = 1,00,000, Kid = 15,000, Elder = 20,000, x = 5,000.

2024: total = 1,10,000; Kid = 20% = 22,000 (11,000 one app, 11,000 multiple); Elder = 30% = 33,000 (22,000 one app, 11,000 multiple); Others = 55,000.

Answer: A. Multiple-app users in 2024 are at least Kid 11,000 + Elder 11,000 = 22,000. The 55,000 ‘Others’ have no constraint, so all of them may use one app. Minimum = 22,000/1,10,000 = 20%.

questions.stemHtml: Which one among the countries 1 through 8, has the smallest population in 2024?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key idea. Population = GDP ÷ GDP per capita. Since both columns are fractions of fixed references (Country 9’s GDP and Country 10’s per-capita GDP), population is proportional to (column 2) ÷ (column 3).

2024 relative populations: C1 0.15/0.41 ≈ 0.366, C2 0.56, C3 6.5, C4 ≈ 0.316, C5 ≈ 0.278, C6 1.0, C7 ≈ 0.267, C8 ≈ 0.171.

Answer: A. Country 8 has the smallest ratio, 0.07/0.41 ≈ 0.171.

questions.stemHtml: The ratio of Country 4’s GDP to Country 5’s GDP in 2026 will be closest to
questions.solutionHtml:
Step 1: In 2024 the ratio is 0.12/0.10 = 1.2.

Step 2: 2026 is two years later: ratio = 1.2 × (1.005/1.007)2 ≈ 1.2 × (0.99801)2 ≈ 1.2 × 0.99602 ≈ 1.195.

Answer: B. (Growth rates differ by only 0.2%, so the ratio falls only slightly below 1.2.)

questions.stemHtml: Which one among the countries 1, 4, 5, and 7 will have the largest population in 2027?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key idea. Population = GDP ÷ GDP per capita. Since both columns are fractions of fixed references (Country 9’s GDP and Country 10’s per-capita GDP), population is proportional to (column 2) ÷ (column 3).

2024 relative populations: C1 0.15/0.41 ≈ 0.366, C2 0.56, C3 6.5, C4 ≈ 0.316, C5 ≈ 0.278, C6 1.0, C7 ≈ 0.267, C8 ≈ 0.171.

Three years of growth: C1 0.366 × (0.9988)3 ≈ 0.365; C4 0.316 × (1.0049)3 ≈ 0.321; C5 0.278 × (1.0031)3 ≈ 0.280; C7 0.267 × (0.9989)3 ≈ 0.266.

Growth rates under 0.5% a year cannot close gaps of 10%+ in three years.

Answer: D. Country 1 remains the largest.

questions.stemHtml: For how many countries among Country 1 through Country 8 will the GDP per capita in 2027 be lower than that in 2024?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key idea: GDP per capita falls only if population grows faster than GDP, i.e. population growth rate > GDP growth rate.

Compare columns 4 and 5: C1 0.2% vs −0.12%; C2 0.9% vs −0.41%; C3 6.5% vs 0.70%; C4 0.5% vs 0.49%; C5 0.7% vs 0.31%; C6 3.2% vs 0.61%; C7 0.7% vs −0.11%; C8 1.2% vs 0.71%.

In every country GDP grows faster than population (Country 4 only just: 0.5% > 0.49%), so GDP per capita rises everywhere.

Answer: 0.

questions.stemHtml: How many times the AC must have been turned off between 11:01 pm and 1:59 am?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. The AC can only cool, so the rising stretches (00:00–00:30 and 01:00–01:30) mean the AC was off; it was switched off at 00:00 and at 01:00 and switched on again at 00:30 and 01:30.

When off, the room heats at a rate that reaches the outside temperature (at switch-off) in 1 hour. 26 → 31 in 30 min means it would reach 36 in an hour: outside = 36 °C at 00:00. 26 → 30 in 30 min: outside = 34 °C at 01:00. So the outside temperature falls 2 °C per hour (38 °C at 23:00, matching the inside reading when the AC was first switched on).

AC-on time = 23:00–00:00 (1 h) + 00:30–01:00 + 01:30–02:00 = 2 h. If the first hour were entirely REGULAR, POWER could be at most 1 h – not longer than REGULAR. So POWER must be used in the first hour, which (because POWER reaches its set point in 30 min and the line falls steadily all hour) needs a setting change at 23:30 (e.g. POWER to 32 then POWER to 26).

Answer: B. Inside temperature rises only when the AC is off: from 00:00 and from 01:00. So it was turned off exactly twice.

questions.stemHtml: What was the temperature outside, in degree Celsius, at 1 am?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. The AC can only cool, so the rising stretches (00:00–00:30 and 01:00–01:30) mean the AC was off; it was switched off at 00:00 and at 01:00 and switched on again at 00:30 and 01:30.

When off, the room heats at a rate that reaches the outside temperature (at switch-off) in 1 hour. 26 → 31 in 30 min means it would reach 36 in an hour: outside = 36 °C at 00:00. 26 → 30 in 30 min: outside = 34 °C at 01:00. So the outside temperature falls 2 °C per hour (38 °C at 23:00, matching the inside reading when the AC was first switched on).

AC-on time = 23:00–00:00 (1 h) + 00:30–01:00 + 01:30–02:00 = 2 h. If the first hour were entirely REGULAR, POWER could be at most 1 h – not longer than REGULAR. So POWER must be used in the first hour, which (because POWER reaches its set point in 30 min and the line falls steadily all hour) needs a setting change at 23:30 (e.g. POWER to 32 then POWER to 26).

Answer: 34. Switched off at 01:00 at 26 °C, the room reaches 30 °C at 01:30, i.e. 4 °C per half hour, so it would reach 34 °C in one hour – the outside temperature at 01:00.

questions.stemHtml: What was the temperature outside, in degree Celsius, at 9 pm?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. The AC can only cool, so the rising stretches (00:00–00:30 and 01:00–01:30) mean the AC was off; it was switched off at 00:00 and at 01:00 and switched on again at 00:30 and 01:30.

When off, the room heats at a rate that reaches the outside temperature (at switch-off) in 1 hour. 26 → 31 in 30 min means it would reach 36 in an hour: outside = 36 °C at 00:00. 26 → 30 in 30 min: outside = 34 °C at 01:00. So the outside temperature falls 2 °C per hour (38 °C at 23:00, matching the inside reading when the AC was first switched on).

AC-on time = 23:00–00:00 (1 h) + 00:30–01:00 + 01:30–02:00 = 2 h. If the first hour were entirely REGULAR, POWER could be at most 1 h – not longer than REGULAR. So POWER must be used in the first hour, which (because POWER reaches its set point in 30 min and the line falls steadily all hour) needs a setting change at 23:30 (e.g. POWER to 32 then POWER to 26).

Answer: 42. Outside was 36 °C at 00:00 and 34 °C at 01:00 – falling 2 °C per hour at a constant rate. Three hours before midnight: 36 + 3 × 2 = 42 °C.

questions.stemHtml: What best can be concluded about the number of times the AC must have either been turned on or the AC temperature setting been altered between 11:01 pm and 1:59 am?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. The AC can only cool, so the rising stretches (00:00–00:30 and 01:00–01:30) mean the AC was off; it was switched off at 00:00 and at 01:00 and switched on again at 00:30 and 01:30.

When off, the room heats at a rate that reaches the outside temperature (at switch-off) in 1 hour. 26 → 31 in 30 min means it would reach 36 in an hour: outside = 36 °C at 00:00. 26 → 30 in 30 min: outside = 34 °C at 01:00. So the outside temperature falls 2 °C per hour (38 °C at 23:00, matching the inside reading when the AC was first switched on).

AC-on time = 23:00–00:00 (1 h) + 00:30–01:00 + 01:30–02:00 = 2 h. If the first hour were entirely REGULAR, POWER could be at most 1 h – not longer than REGULAR. So POWER must be used in the first hour, which (because POWER reaches its set point in 30 min and the line falls steadily all hour) needs a setting change at 23:30 (e.g. POWER to 32 then POWER to 26).

Answer: D. Required events: setting change at 23:30, AC turned on at 00:30, AC turned on at 01:30. The remaining stretches (00:30–01:00 and 01:30–02:00) can each be done with one POWER setting, so nothing more is forced. Exactly 3.

questions.stemHtml: What was the maximum difference between temperature outside and inside temperature, in degree Celsius, between 11:01 pm and 1:59 am?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. The AC can only cool, so the rising stretches (00:00–00:30 and 01:00–01:30) mean the AC was off; it was switched off at 00:00 and at 01:00 and switched on again at 00:30 and 01:30.

When off, the room heats at a rate that reaches the outside temperature (at switch-off) in 1 hour. 26 → 31 in 30 min means it would reach 36 in an hour: outside = 36 °C at 00:00. 26 → 30 in 30 min: outside = 34 °C at 01:00. So the outside temperature falls 2 °C per hour (38 °C at 23:00, matching the inside reading when the AC was first switched on).

AC-on time = 23:00–00:00 (1 h) + 00:30–01:00 + 01:30–02:00 = 2 h. If the first hour were entirely REGULAR, POWER could be at most 1 h – not longer than REGULAR. So POWER must be used in the first hour, which (because POWER reaches its set point in 30 min and the line falls steadily all hour) needs a setting change at 23:30 (e.g. POWER to 32 then POWER to 26).

Outside: 38 at 23:00, 37 at 23:30, 36 at 00:00, 35 at 00:30, 34 at 01:00, 33 at 01:30. Inside: 38, 32, 26, 31, 26, 30.

Differences at the turning points: 5 (23:30), 10 (00:00), 4 (00:30), 8 (01:00), 3 (01:30). Both curves are straight between these points, so the maximum is at a turning point.

Answer: 10.

questions.stemHtml: How many foodgrains had a higher amount of carbohydrate per 100 grams of nutrients than M1?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions (each row sums to 100; missing carbs are multiples of 5, other missing values multiples of 4).
